_doc: Pool-driven uniques: items whose mods are a CRAFTABLE POOL rather than a fixed
stat block. Path of Building's unique data format is (name, one base, fixed mod
list), so it cannot represent these items at all — they are simply absent from
pob-uniques/*.json, and since scripts/graph/uniques.js enumerates unique nodes
FROM PoB, they got no node and vanished from the site silently.
RePoE has everything needed except the join: uniques.json carries the metadata
(icon, inventory size, item class) and mods.json carries the full mod pool. The
only irreducible hand-authored facts are in this file — which vid is the item,
which mod-id prefix is its pool, and the honest note about what is NOT known.
Everything else (mod display text, icon, flavour, edges) is builder-derived.
HONESTY RULE: the game data does NOT record how many pool mods a finished item
receives, nor how they are selected. Do not add a count or formula here unless a
table actually states it. Every `note` must make clear the pool is what the item
CAN have, not what any single copy DOES have.

entries._baseLabelWhy: ItemVisualIdentity[15276] ships AO art for all six attribute combos (LoreweaveStr/Dex/Int/StrDex/StrInt/DexInt), i.e. it is not bound to one base. RePoE gives no base for it either (uniques.json has no base field).
note: Woven by Dannig in the Ruins of Kingmarch from unique Rings. Requires the recipe book *One Hundred Ways to Weave a Lore*; the exchange window has 60 ring slots.
Every mod below is one Loreweave **can** have — this is the whole pool, not one item's mods. How many a finished Loreweave receives, and how they are chosen, are **not recorded in the game data**.

_noteEvidence.Dannig: NPCTalkDialogue 'DannigLoreweave' + ClientStrings ItemFunctionLoreweaveBook = 'Can be brought to Dannig in the Ruins of Kingmarch'
_noteEvidence.count unknown: ring count is a runtime value in both strings ('{0}/{1}', 'Requires {0} additional'); no table states the output mod count or selection rule

note: Every mod below is one Grip of Kulemak **can** have, not what any single copy does have. How many it receives, and how they are chosen, are **not recorded in the game data**.
entries._vidWhy: RePoE lists FIVE non-alternate-art vids for this name (FourUniqueRing33_a..__e); _a is pinned as canonical. If RePoE re-scrapes with different suffixes the vid guardrail fails the build rather than silently mis-joining.
entries._modPrefixWhy: INFERRED. The only Kulemak mods anywhere in RePoE mods.json are UniqueLoreweaveKulemak1..15 (+BigRange twins) — there is no separate non-Loreweave Kulemak mod set. Attributing them to the ring is the only reading available, but it is an inference from the id naming, not a stated relationship. The note wording stays hedged accordingly.

note: Flesh Crucible exacts a **price**. Every line below is a price it can carry; which one a given jewel has is **not recorded in the game data**.
entries._modPrefixWhy: Internal name differs from display name: this jewel's art is Art/2DItems/Jewels/Uniques/Vivisection.dds, and its mods are UniqueVivisectionPrice{Life,Mana,Defences,Spirit,MovementSpeed,Damage}1. Searching mods.json by DISPLAY name finds nothing — that is why this one was first mistaken for a data hole. Always search by the art/vid stem too.
entries._excludes: UniqueMutatedVaalVivisectionPrice* are the Vaal-cultivated twins of the same six prices and are handled by the cultivated-uniques overlay, not here — the UniqueVivisectionPrice prefix deliberately does not match them.

_sourceUniquesDoc: Loreweave mod ids encode the unique ring each woven mod came from:
UniqueLoreweaveSnakepit1 -> Snakepit. That mapping is what makes the pool
traversable — every pooled mod links to its source unique, and each ring page
gains a reverse 'weaves into Loreweave' lookup via edgesTo(id,'pool_source').
internal stem -> display name. Listed EXHAUSTIVELY on purpose (not as a rule):
the stem->name mapping is irreducible and cannot be derived, and an explicit
list means a GGG rename fails the build loudly instead of silently dropping the
relationship. Precedent for why that matters: SekhemasResolve is displayed as
"Safrin's Resolve" — GGG renamed the item and kept the old internal id.
null = deliberately UNATTRIBUTED. Safrin's Resolve is Ruby-only, so the Emerald
and Sapphire jewel-restriction mods belong to sibling rings that are not in our
data. Those mods still appear in the pool, just with no origin link — better
than asserting an origin we cannot support.
